item.title: 92 communities without water as drought worsens across Fiji
item.description: A total of 92 communities across Fiji have no water supply, while 372 communities are experiencing critical water levels and 244 are approaching critical levels, according to assessments of 733 communities amid worsening drought conditions. Permanent Secretary for Rural and Maritime Development and National Disaster Controller Mitieli Cama highlights this during an update on the Government's natio
item.content:encoded:
A total of 92 communities across Fiji have no water supply, while 372 communities are experiencing critical water levels and 244 are approaching critical levels, according to assessments of 733 communities amid worsening drought conditions.

Permanent Secretary for Rural and Maritime Development and National Disaster Controller Mitieli Cama highlights this during an update on the Government's national El Niño drought response.

Cama says the latest assessments show the scale of the challenge facing the country and the urgent need for a coordinated response to ensure assistance reaches communities most affected by the drought.

He says the Fiji Meteorological Service confirms that El Niño conditions remain strong, with conditions expected to peak around December this year.

Below-normal rain is also likely to continue into early 2027, meaning the drought emergency could extend beyond the peak El Niño period.

Cama says the Water Authority of Fiji has reported that approximately 61.36 percent of monitored water sources have reached critical levels.

Following the declaration of a National State of Disaster on 18th November, the Government has strengthened coordination through the National Disaster Risk Management Office and the National Emergency Operations Centre.

He says divisional, provincial and district emergency operations centres will also play a key role in coordinating assistance, ensuring resources are properly allocated and avoiding duplication of support.

He says Government agencies and their partners are stepping up emergency water carting, borehole activation, the development of alternative water sources and water treatment initiatives.

Cama says protecting essential services is also a priority, with water supplies to hospitals, health centres and schools being prioritised.

Agencies are also strengthening water storage and emergency supply arrangements, implementing conservation measures and maintaining alternative electricity generation capacity to reduce reliance on hydroelectric power.

Cama says the National Emergency Committee, which met on Monday, also supported proposals for schools to conclude all activities by this Friday.

All sporting activities, competitions, tournaments and other school events will also be cancelled during the closure period.

He says the proposed measures aim to reduce pressure on water supply systems and allow available water resources to be redirected towards communities and other priority needs.

Cama says the Government is also strengthening public awareness of water conservation and assessing possible restrictions on car washing, commercial water use, social gatherings and sporting events.

These measures are still being assessed for their legal, operational and socio-economic implications, with further updates expected once the assessments are completed.

The Ministry of Health and relevant agencies are also strengthening disease surveillance and preparedness in affected communities while promoting safe drinking water, sanitation and hygiene to prevent water-related diseases.

The Government is also monitoring the needs of vulnerable households, particularly women, children, older persons and people with disabilities.

Cama says the drought is also affecting electricity generation, with Energy Fiji Limited reporting declining hydropower reserves and making arrangements to strengthen standby generation capacity, including additional generators where required.

In the agriculture sector, six drought response initiatives have been identified to support water access, irrigation, the protection of agricultural livelihoods and recovery efforts.

He says the drought is not only a water supply issue but also has implications for food security, household income, agricultural production and the wider economy.

Cama is urging all Fijians, businesses and institutions to conserve water, avoid unnecessary use and prioritise water for drinking, cooking and essential hygiene.

He is also asking the public to report serious water shortages to the relevant authorities, follow official advisories and avoid activities that could trigger grass fires and bushfires.

Cama says people should also look out for vulnerable members of their communities as the Government continues to coordinate assistance based on verified needs and the severity of the situation.

He says the declaration of the National State of Disaster reflects the seriousness of the drought and the need for a coordinated response from the Government and the wider community.

item.title: Consumer Council receives 12 complaints about bed bugs in accommodations across Fiji
item.description: The Consumer Council of Fiji has received 12 complaints about bed bugs in accommodation facilities across the country so far this year. The complaints involve small hotels, homestays, Airbnb properties and large resorts.
item.content:encoded:
The Consumer Council of Fiji has received 12 complaints about bed bugs in accommodation facilities across the country so far this year.

The complaints involve small hotels, homestays, Airbnb properties and large resorts.

The Council says six of the 12 complaints have been received since the beginning of October, accounting for half of all complaints recorded this year.

It believes the actual number of affected guests could be higher, as many people may not formally report their experiences.

In one case involving a hotel in Nadi, a guest was severely bitten by bed bugs and moved to another room, only to discover bed bugs there as well.

Consumer Council CEO Seema Shandil says guests have the right to expect a clean room and a comfortable night's sleep when they pay for accommodation.

She says simply moving guests to another room is not enough unless the room has been properly inspected.

Shandil is urging hotels, resorts and other accommodation providers to carry out regular pest inspections and arrange professional treatment when bed bugs are found.

She says affected rooms should be taken out of service until they have been professionally treated and inspected.

The Council is also advising guests who encounter bed bugs to report the issue immediately, take photographs and keep their booking confirmations, receipts and any communication with the accommodation provider.

Consumers can contact the Council on 155 or email complaints@consumersfiji.org.

item.title: Firefighters bring Denarau house fire under control
item.description: A house fire broke out on Denarau Island in Nadi this afternoon. The Nadi Fire Authority has confirmed to fijivillage News that firefighters have brought the blaze under control.
item.content:encoded:
A house fire broke out on Denarau Island in Nadi this afternoon.

The Nadi Fire Authority has confirmed to fijivillage News that firefighters have brought the blaze under control.

Fortunately, no injuries have been reported.
